name: Scheme
typeSystem: Dynamic, strong; a minimalist Lisp dialect built from a small set of core special forms, with lexical scoping and first-class, re-entrant continuations (call/cc) as its most distinctive feature.
runtime: Implementations range from simple tree-walking interpreters to optimising native-code compilers; the standard guarantees proper tail calls as a language feature, not merely an optional optimisation.

runtimes.name: Chez Scheme
runtimes.role: High-performance native-code compiler; also embedded as the backend of modern Racket.

runtimes.name: Chicken Scheme
runtimes.role: Compiles Scheme to C, then to native code, with extensive library support.

runtimes.name: Guile
runtimes.role: GNU's embeddable Scheme; Guile 3 compiles through bytecode and, on supported targets, transparently JIT-compiles hot code to native code.

compilers.name: Chicken (csc)
compilers.role: Compiles Scheme to C for native compilation.

concurrencyModel: Implementation-dependent: many Schemes provide green threads or native OS threads as a library feature, and call/cc lets user code build its own coroutines and generators directly.
